sources.title: United States Census, 1850, Pottsville, Schuylkill, Pennsylvania

entry.rationale: Review pending FamilySearch hints on ZZKR-TH2 before searching — an attached hint may already answer the question.

The FamilySearch tree (not the project tree) attaches a christening of 14 Mar 1842 at St. Patrick's Church, Pottsville, from 'Pennsylvania, Catholic Church Records, 1750-1950', and names Patrick Kerrigan and Mary Gallagher as parents. Treat these as leads to verify, not conclusions. Pull the baptismal entry itself and read the parents' names and sponsors. The Schuylkill church collection is name-searchable; loc_001 notes Catholic registers stay with the parish and the Philadelphia diocese, so confirm against the register image. Try variant spellings (Kerrigan, Kerragan, Kerrican, Carrigan).

Fallback if the indexed church search misses or mis-transcribes the entry: browse the church-records image group, which is browse-only (personCount 0) and quirk-flagged in loc_001 as image-by-image. Look for the 1842 St. Patrick's baptism and later Kerrigan sacraments.

The FamilySearch tree cites an 1850 census for Thomas at Pottsville. The 1850 census is the first to name every household member and record birthplace, so it can place Thomas (about 8) in a household with Patrick and Mary. It does not state relationships, so it supports but cannot alone prove parentage. Note neighbors for FAN leads.

Follow the Kerrigan household across 1860, 1870 and 1880 to cover the window to Patrick's reported death in 1880. The 1880 census records relationship to head and parents' birthplaces, the best census test of Thomas as Patrick's son, and shows whether Mary was still living.

Dedicated item for the candidate parents' marriage to each other (Patrick Kerrigan and Mary Gallagher, per the FamilySearch tree lead): it would confirm them as a couple, give the mother's name, and its date relative to 1842 corroborates but does not by itself prove Thomas is their child. Mary's Gallagher surname may be a prior married name, so it is not assumed to be her maiden name. Statewide civil registration began 1906 and the county marriage collections begin 1885, so search the name-searchable church records and compiled marriages. The marriage may have taken place in Ireland (Patrick reportedly born County Mayo about 1815), so also check Irish records.

Patrick Kerrigan reportedly died 1880 in Pottsville (FamilySearch tree lead). A will or estate file would name heirs including Thomas. The probate collection is browse-only (personCount 0) and a separate Schuylkill probate image group covers 1851-1930, so browse image by image. Window follows the parent's lifespan; a mother's later estate may also fall in it.

Thomas's own death and burial (1898, before the 1906 statewide death registration) and Patrick's 1880 burial. Catholic burial entries, cemetery records and an obituary may give age, birthplace or parents. This is a back-up route to the origin should the baptism not name the parents clearly. Check Find a Grave and local newspapers.

FAN and sibling item: baptisms and marriages of Thomas's possible siblings, plus the sponsors on the 1842 baptism. Records naming the same Patrick and Mary would show the family unit, and sponsors are often kin. Also search Thomas's own marriage to Ellen Burke, about 1870, which may name parents.

Patrick, if born in Ireland about 1815, may have naturalized. The Schuylkill naturalization image group is browse-only (personCount 0). A declaration could give his arrival date, origin and family. Lower priority.

## Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania - 1840-1900

Schuylkill County (formed 1811 from Berks and Northampton) lies in Pennsylvania's anthracite coal region. Deed/land records are held by the county Recorder of Deeds from 1811; much coal-region land was leased from mining companies rather than purchased outright. Catholic parishes stayed with the Diocese (from 1875 the Archdiocese) of Philadelphia until the Diocese of Allentown was erected in 1961. Statewide civil vital registration began only in 1906 -- pre-1906 events are recorded in church, cemetery, and probate records instead. Some coal-region naturalization and church films are browse-only. Curated external links reach county tax and exoneration lists for 1768-1801 only, before this period.

entry.rationale: Review pending FamilySearch hints on ZZKR-BR1 before searching — an attached hint may already answer the question.

The tree records only Bridget's 1871 Pottsville birth and no baptism. Her parents Thomas Kerrigan (b. 1842 Pottsville) and Ellen Burke (b. 1846 Ireland) were probably Irish Catholic, so a baptism within weeks of birth is expected. 'Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records' is name-searchable; search Bridget with variants Kerrigan/Kerrigen/Kerigan/Carrigan/Kerrighan and Bridget/Bridgit/Biddy/Brigid, plus parents Thomas and Ellen (Burke/Bourke). Birth was only given as a year, so search 1870-1873 and do not filter by parish.

Fallback for the name search: the church-record image volume for Schuylkill County is browse-only (personCount 0, 0% record-searchable) and includes German-language material. Per loc_001, coal-region church films are often browse-only, so browse image by image the Catholic baptism registers of Pottsville parishes for 1871. Sacramental registers stay with the parish and the Archdiocese of Philadelphia (Schuylkill was never in the Scranton diocese), not the county.

FAN item: baptisms of Bridget's siblings (children of Thomas Kerrigan and Ellen Burke) and their sponsors, found in the same name-searchable church collection. They identify the family's parish and the usual priest and godparents, and so point to the right register for Bridget even if her own entry is misindexed. Window runs from the parents' probable marriage (about 1865) to the last likely child.

The 1880 census names every household member with relationship to the head, giving Bridget's siblings' names and ages and Ellen's birthplace. That sharpens the baptism search (birth month/year, sibling names) and shows neighbors who may have been sponsors. It does not itself prove a baptism.

No baptism may survive or be indexed, and statewide civil registration began only in 1906 (loc_001), so nothing civil exists for 1871. Bridget's own death certificate (if she died after 1906; 'Pennsylvania, Death Certificates, 1906-1968' is name-searchable) gives exact birth date and place and parents' names, which narrow the register search; burial place suggests her parish. Size window to her life, not the 1871 event.

FAN item: father Thomas Kerrigan died 1898 in Pottsville per the tree. His Catholic burial entry, funeral notice or obituary in a local newspaper or Catholic cemetery record names his parish, pointing to the family's church and its registers.

Last resort if neither the index nor the film images yield the entry: request a baptismal certificate search from the parish registers of the Pottsville Catholic parish identified by items 4 and 7, or the Archdiocese of Philadelphia archives, since registers are held at the parish/archdiocese.

Pennsylvania statewide civil birth/death registration did not begin until 1906; a 1908 death has a state certificate, but pre-1906 events rely on church, cemetery, and probate records.
